paragraphs: Friend, here's the verdict on Amaziah: he did what was right in the eyes of the LORD, but not wholeheartedly (2 Chronicles 25:2). Look at how that plays out. He follows the Law of Moses when it comes to the murderers' sons (2 Chronicles 25:4). Then he comes home from a win and sets up the gods of Seir as his own (2 Chronicles 25:14). A half-hearted yes to God is still a half-hearted yes, and it shows up exactly when the pressure and the victory hit.

Now notice what God gives Amaziah along the way: a man of God who tells him the LORD is not with Israel, and a promise that "The LORD is able to give you much more than this" (2 Chronicles 25:9). Amaziah listens when it costs him a hundred talents. Then a prophet asks why he would seek gods that "could not deliver" their own people from him, and Amaziah says, "Stop!" (2 Chronicles 25:15-16). Friend, I have been a quarter in a bin. I know what it is to count the cost. But listening to God only when it's easy is not the same as trusting Him.

So here's the big idea, baker. God doesn't want the part of us that's convenient. He wants all of it, and that includes the day after the win, when we feel strong and nobody's asking. The prophet's last word is a hard one: God "has determined to destroy" Amaziah because he did this and did not heed the advice (2 Chronicles 25:16). Ask yourself where you've been giving God a yes with a catch. Then bring Him the whole batch, and I'll keep the ovens warm for you.
